sections.h2: Where is Paragould, and how is the city laid out?
sections.html:
Paragould is the county seat of Greene County in northeastern Arkansas, and it is the 15th-largest city in the state. It sits on the eastern edge of Crowley's Ridge, a line of higher ground that rises out of the flat Arkansas Delta.

The city covers a little over 32 square miles, and its elevation is about 289 feet. U.S. 412 and U.S. 49 cross just west of downtown. Highway 412 runs about 9 miles east to the Missouri line at the St. Francis River, and U.S. 49 runs roughly 20 miles southwest to Jonesboro. Memphis is the nearest major city, about 82 miles to the southeast.

For a seller, the practical point is access. Two federal routes and a short drive to Jonesboro and the Missouri line make Paragould workable for commuters, and that is worth mentioning to any buyer.

sections.h2: How did Paragould get its name and start growing?
sections.html:
Paragould exists because two railroads crossed here in 1882: the Texas & St. Louis Railway, later the Cotton Belt, and the St. Louis, Iron Mountain and Southern, later the Missouri Pacific. The name joins the surnames of two railroad figures, J. W. Paramore and Jay Gould, and the town is believed to be the only one with that name anywhere.

In 1888 the town became the starting point of the Paragould and Buffalo Island Railway, which later reached Blytheville. Greene County moved its seat to Paragould in 1883, and the county courthouse built in 1888 still stands downtown.

A town that dates to the 1880s has houses of many ages. When we look at an older Paragould house, the questions are usually about the roof, the foundation, the electrical panel and the plumbing, since those are the systems that age first.

sections.h2: What do Paragould's weather numbers mean for a house?
sections.html:
Paragould has a humid subtropical climate, which means hot, wet summers and short, mild winters. The 1991 to 2020 normals show a July mean daily high of 89.8 degrees and a January mean daily high of 45.7 degrees.

The city averages 51.74 inches of precipitation a year across about 115 days, and only about 2.5 inches of snow. Recorded extremes run from 106 degrees to minus 14 degrees.

  • Air conditioning does most of the work from late spring into early fall, so the age of the condenser and ductwork is a real value item.
  • Fifty-plus inches of rain a year puts pressure on roofs, gutters, grading and crawl space vents.
  • Occasional hard freezes make exposed pipes and old water heaters a repair risk.

Deferred maintenance in any of these systems is the usual reason a Paragould owner decides to sell as-is instead of paying for repairs first.

The city grew by about 3,400 people in the 2010s, which is steady growth for a Delta-region county seat. Greene County itself is 580 square miles and borders Clay, Craighead, Lawrence and Randolph counties in Arkansas, plus Dunklin County, Missouri.

sections.h2: Which utilities and schools serve a Paragould home?
sections.html:
Paragould Light, Water and Cable, a municipally owned utility, provides electric service inside the city, along with water from its own wells, sewer treatment and cable broadband. A fiber internet build is also under way in phases. Natural gas comes from CenterPoint Energy. Outside the city limits, Craighead Electric or Entergy Arkansas serve parts of Greene County, and rural water associations cover some areas.

That split matters when a seller lists a house just outside town. Buyers should confirm which provider serves the address, because a rural address may not have city water or sewer at all.

Two public districts serve the area: the Paragould School District, formed in 1985 by merging with Oak Grove and renamed in 1997, and the Greene County Tech School District. Private options include Crowley's Ridge Academy and St. Mary's Catholic School. Higher education includes Crowley's Ridge College and a Black River Technical College campus. A Paragould address does not always tell you which district a home is in, so sellers should check the district map before advertising a school.

sections.h2: How do property taxes work when a Paragould house sells?
sections.html:
Greene County bills Paragould real estate tax, and the county collector is at 320 West Court Street in Paragould. The collector's page says taxes become payable on March 1, when the books open, and the deadline to pay without penalty is October 15. Real estate left unpaid after that date carries a 10% penalty plus a daily fee. The office is open Monday through Friday, 8:00 AM to 4:30 PM, and you can pay online, by phone or at the counter.

The state sets the rules for how the county values a house. According to the Arkansas Department of Finance and Administration, properties are reappraised every 3, 4 or 5 years. If you disagree with a value, start with the county assessor, because simple errors in square footage or room counts can often be fixed without a hearing. For a formal appeal, the deadline to schedule a hearing with the County Board of Equalization is the third Monday in August.

  • The homestead tax credit is up to $500 a year, rising to up to $600 beginning with 2026 tax bills.
  • Under Amendment 79, a homestead's taxable value can rise no more than 5% a year, and other real property is limited to 10% a year.
  • The caps do not apply to new construction or substantial improvements that add at least 25% to value.

A buyer does not inherit a seller's age 65 or disability freeze, so an older owner with a low taxable value should expect the next owner's bill to look different.

sections.h2: What does Arkansas require at a Paragould closing?
sections.html:
Arkansas charges a real estate transfer tax of $3.30 for every $1,000 of actual consideration on deeds over $100, and the state sells the tax as a stamp that is purchased at recording. The statute text on Justia lists a base rate of $1.10 per $1,000 and an additional $2.20 per $1,000 that it says is to be paid by the purchaser, so who pays what is something to settle in the contract.

Arkansas does not require every seller to disclose every known defect. The Arkansas Real Estate Commission says the Seller Property Disclosure form from the Arkansas Realtors Association is not legally mandated, although Realtors encourage sellers to complete it. If no agent is involved, disclosure duties come from the contract the two sides sign.

In practice, a Paragould seller should still write down known problems such as roof leaks, past water in the crawl space or a failed inspection. A clear list protects the seller later and speeds up a cash sale.

sections.h2: What are the realistic ways to sell a Paragould house?
sections.html:
A Paragould owner has three paths: list with an agent, sell privately, or accept a cash offer from a buyer who purchases the house as it stands. Each one trades time, cost and certainty differently.

  • Listing with an agent: exposure to financed buyers, but showings, repairs requested after inspection, appraisal timing and a commission to pay.
  • Selling privately: no commission, but you handle pricing, paperwork, the transfer stamp and any buyer questions yourself.
  • Cash sale: an as-is purchase with no financing contingency, which suits inherited houses, tenant-occupied houses and homes that need work.

Whichever route you choose, gather the last tax statement, any utility account details from Paragould Light, Water and Cable, and the deed before you talk to a buyer. Those three items answer most early questions.

faqs.q: How many people live in Paragould?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau estimates 31,135 residents as of July 1, 2025. The city counted 29,537 people in the 2020 census and 26,113 in 2010.

faqs.q: When are Greene County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Greene County taxes can be paid starting March 1, and they are due without penalty by October 15. Real estate taxes left unpaid after that date carry a 10% penalty plus a daily fee, according to the county collector.

faqs.q: Who provides electricity and water in Paragould?
faqs.a: Paragould Light, Water and Cable provides electricity, water, sewer and cable broadband inside city limits. CenterPoint Energy supplies natural gas, and rural addresses may be served by Craighead Electric, Entergy Arkansas or a rural water association.

faqs.q: Do Arkansas sellers have to fill out a disclosure form?
faqs.a: No state law requires every seller to complete a disclosure form. The Arkansas Realtors Association form is encouraged but not mandatory, and sellers who skip it can still be held to the terms of the sale contract.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Paragould house that needs repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. You can list it, sell it yourself or sell it as-is to a cash buyer. Repairs only need to be done if a financed buyer's lender or inspection requires them.
